A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Sokoban DRC study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison despite the changed title and extensive reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original channel interventions, state and gate ablations, backtracking experiments, and weight-steering results, including Table 2 and Appendices D, I, and M.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds training-checkpoint and cross-seed analyses in Appendices M and N.

M1.justification: Appendix N introduces automatic channel labeling using AUC thresholds across directions, spatial offsets, activation signs, and prediction horizons, replacing manual labeling for the additional networks. The underlying DRC architecture, training objective, and principal planning mechanisms are retained.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Boxoban training and held-out difficulty categories and the same custom path-choice, zig-zag, and larger backtracking levels. Additional training checkpoints and network seeds extend model analysis without adding datasets or task scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same box-movement and agent-movement probe comparisons. v1 Table 9 and v2 Table 10 contain the same DRC(3,3), DRC(1,1), and ResNet comparisons; the base-feature regression control also remains.

E3.justification: Appendix M adds checkpoint-wise evaluation throughout the existing two-billion-step training run using self-connection, cross-inhibition, and normalized WTA metrics. Appendix N adds F1 evaluation of automatic labeling. Existing dataset splits, intervention sample sizes, and benchmark thinking budgets are retained.

E4.justification: New Appendices M and N investigate when WTA structure emerges and whether channel representations and planning kernels recur across four additional training seeds. Figures 25–26 add individual-kernel inspection. These substantially extend the mechanistic validation beyond the retained ablations and case studies.

E5.justification: Reported seed coverage expands from one analyzed network to five independently trained networks. v2 also adds uncertainty estimates to the previously bare cache-ablation drops: 10.5±1.9%, 57.6±2.8%, and 41.3±2.4% in Table 3. Their interval interpretation is unspecified; existing intervention uncertainties and Appendix I's 95% confidence intervals remain unchanged.

E6.justification: v2 newly reports WTA emergence around 19 million training steps, automatic channel-discovery F1 of 73.7%, cross-seed channel counts in Table 4, and additional kernel findings. These supplement unchanged intervention scores, regression correlations, and benchmark solve rates in the corresponding retained tables.

T1.justification: Appendix M introduces the normalized WTA definition (self-cross)/(|self|+|cross|) and its bounded-range interpretation. Appendix B also corrects the encoder expression from using WE2 twice in v1 Equation 1 to WE1 followed by WE2 in v2 Equation 3. Most remaining mathematics is retained or re-notated.

C1.justification: v2 narrows the headline emphasis to path channels and specific transition-model components, presenting the value/Q-function interpretation more tentatively in the discussion. Its introduction also explicitly claims replication across four additional networks. The central bidirectional planning, backtracking, and WTA claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 newly attributes probes' weaker causal effects to spurious correlations and elaborates the Q-function analogy's limitations, including biased WTA selection. Cross-seed stability replaces the single-network generalization caveat. Architecture/task restrictions and unexplained box-switching and heuristic behaviors remain in Appendix P.

D1.justification: v2 specifies automatic-labeling thresholds, horizons, tick choices, run identifiers, and kernel-averaging conventions, but removes the standalone techniques overview and direct-effect definition. It also introduces a documentation conflict: Section 3.2 credits steering by 1.4 with success, while Appendix L retains successful steering by 1.2 and Figure 18 shows failure at 1.4.

R1.justification: v2 removes citations associated with the deleted test-time-scaling and methods overviews, including DeepSeek-R1, OpenAI o1, and Conmy et al.'s automated circuit discovery. It more explicitly positions direct channel reading against prior Sokoban probes while retaining the broad mechanistic-interpretability and mesa-optimization positioning.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and concluding discussion are extensively rewritten around path representation and construction. Architecture moves into the representation section, the standalone methods overview disappears, and background material moves to Appendix O. This substantially changes the narrative independently of the added experiments.

P2.justification: The opening overview moves from v1 Figure 1 to v2 Figure 10, while the earlier appendix channel visualization becomes Figure 1. Architecture diagrams are combined, appendix AUC and transfer plots move into the main text, and new checkpoint plots, seed comparisons, and individual-kernel displays substantially reorganize the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses v1's lack of cross-seed validation with four additional networks and adds checkpoint analysis and individual-kernel evidence, strengthening the support and transparency of the mechanistic account. The replication remains primarily structural and uses imperfect automatic labeling, while the new steering-factor statement conflicts with the retained appendix experiment. The evidence supports a limited net improvement.
